title.narrative: Building Resilience of Conflict Affected Communities in Ukraine - Support Basic Needs and Reduce Impact of Future Shocks

description.narrative: (1) Female-headed Households: Female population starting from 30 years old, who might be a widow or take a lead on HH after the husband was conscripted. Especially in rural areas, these households face significant economic challenges, lack labor opportunities, and suffer from low-cost or part-time employment. (2) PWD, Including War Veterans: The group of people starting from 18 years old, who are particularly vulnerable. This group faces daily barriers, low mobility, limited opportunities, and challenges in accessing livelihood and healthcare services. (3) Women and girls face heightened risks of GBV and exploitation, while also grappling with the burden of caregiving responsibilities.(4) Children, including CWD, severe health conditions, mental health issues, survivors of gender-based violence, those experiencing violence in the home and their caregivers.(5) Youth: 18 up to 25 years old, facing a lack of access to knowledge and skill development and has experienced isolation. Many young people have been forced to flee their homes, becoming internally displaced and separating from their support networks, putting them at a heightened risk of psychological trauma. (6) Elderly People: Women and men over 60, vulnerable due to smaller pensions and higher poverty rates. (7) Small-Scale Farmers: small farmers households up to 15 hectares of land with specific focus on female farmers households.(8) IDPs: face unique and compound challenges stemming from displacement and removal from the societal networks and structures they previously depended on.(9) Returnees: Supporting their reintegration is crucial for community stability and economic recovery.(10) Host Community: Vulnerable individuals directly affected by the war. Disruption on education, access to basic services, and overall sense of security and stability.(11) Employees of State Institutions: Nurses and/or feldshers working in these communities will be supported through capacity building, improved working conditions, and incentives.

Outcome 1: Enhanced access to quality health and social services of target communitiesOutcome 2: Strengthened Community Empowerment, and Protection Services for Community StabilityOutcome 3: Enhanced Livelihoods and Economic Opportunities for Sustainable Development

The objective of this intervention is to Strengthen resilience of conflict affected communities in Sumy, Zaporizhzhia and Mykolaiv oblasts enabling them to meet immediate basic needs and reduce negative impacts of future shocks or crises. This will be achieved through targeted training, fostering cooperation among local authorities, businesses, and farmers, developing inclusive strategies for integrating vulnerable groups into the workforce, including people with disabilities, implementing youth soft skills and internship programs, rehabilitation of health facilities, rehabilitation of facilities administrated by social institutions, strengthening media literacy and promote community empowerment. This will be implemented with PIN and IRC.
